title: The answer and the right next step
spoken: An HR question should not become a hunt through Teams, emails and client records. Meet Finn, the SDtrust desktop companion for an answer you can check, or a clear next step.
cues: Open calmly. Introduce the team without adding a separate team slide.

title: Meet Finn
spoken: Finn keeps the interaction small. Ask, see the answer, and open the evidence when needed. If evidence is missing, the experience changes from answering to finding the person who can help.
cues: The question matcher supports the prepared demo questions. Do not suggest arbitrary question coverage. Owner lookup and contact are fixture data.

title: Product demo
spoken: This first prototype uses scripted questions and synthetic records. We ask when Atlas can submit payroll changes. Finn shows the twenty second of October and the approved client agreement. We open the evidence to see why the other dates do not apply. Then we ask: and for next month?

10 to 25 seconds: show 22 October and open View details or Why this source.
25 to 35 seconds: point to S4 and one rejected source.
35 to 45 seconds: ask “And for next month?” and show the evidence gap.

title: Why 22 October applies
spoken: The account owner approved the Atlas agreement for Belgium in October. It overrides the general deadline. The other dates are proposals or recollections. Finn makes that distinction visible, with the source behind the answer.
cues: Use this slide as the first demo fallback. Avoid reading a confidence percentage as calibrated accuracy. The fixture contains 0.92, but this is a scripted score, not an evaluation result.
status: Fixture reasoning and UI source display are present in inspected code. Trust scores and applicability decisions are authored fixture values, not independently computed or validated predictions.

title: The right next step
spoken: For November, Finn does not recycle October’s answer. It shows the missing evidence and identifies Roy, the Atlas owner. Contact is simulated here. A real message and reply loop comes next.
cues: Use this slide as the second demo fallback. Do not say that Finn has actually sent a Teams message. In the fixture, all October sources are no longer applicable to November, including the general rule.
status: The null answer, owner and proposed message are fixture values. The UI explicitly says simulated contact. No external message has been sent.

title: Sick leave example
spoken: In our synthetic sick leave case, the approved procedure says twenty four hours. Forty eight is unconfirmed. Seventy two comes from an expired version. The status of the source matters.
cues: Optional cut if the live demo runs long. These are synthetic fixture policy values, not real Belgian legal requirements. Do not present them as guidance to SD Worx clients.

title: Value and next step
spoken: For SD Worx, everyday expertise becomes easier to use, with uncertainty in view. Next, we would pilot authorised sources and real colleague confirmation in one workflow, measuring time to a supported answer and interruptions to experts. Less searching, with better judgement.
cues: End here within 170 seconds. Leave ten seconds of safety margin. These are proposed pilot metrics, not measured savings. The safe connection and access controls are future pilot requirements, not a claim of a completed security review. Keep the completed Aikido evidence ready separately for submission and questions.
status: Value hypothesis and roadmap. Real connectors, permission enforcement over enterprise sources, ongoing freshness monitoring, colleague replies and knowledge reuse remain future work. Voice is deliberately excluded. No security scan result is asserted.
